failure_question: Which interchange or junction failures can break a statewide service promise because too much movement concentrates through one node?

minimum_inputs: state network graph; interchange inventory; detour graph; incident or closure history

failure_question: If a T1/T2 link fails, how much time, distance, capacity, safety, or service-class penalty does the best alternate impose?
route_product_use: Compare resilience value of state-system alternates versus interstate-only routing
minimum_inputs: tier graph; travel-time model; state-route attributes; closure scenarios; truck restrictions

failure_question: What share of priority promises depends on interstate links when state highways could provide redundancy, access, or load shedding?
route_product_use: Expose where the state system is underused as resilience and access infrastructure
minimum_inputs: candidate promise list; roadway ownership/class; parallel state routes; freight and access constraints

failure_question: Which priority city pairs have a credible non-interstate or mixed-system fallback that can carry a defined minimum service role?
route_product_use: Identify T2/T3 state-highway roles and backup-route proof gaps
minimum_inputs: tier graph; state-route geometry; travel-time model; bridge/weight/height restrictions; seasonal restrictions

failure_question: Which ports, airports, intermodal yards, hospitals, campuses, industrial parks, or downtowns fail because the last mile is not part of the service network?
route_product_use: Build T4 access backlog and terminal proof docket
minimum_inputs: terminal inventory; truck routes; access constraints; local bottleneck evidence; stakeholder intake

failure_question: Which rural regions lose practical service when a trunk or connector fails because the alternate path is too long, fragile, or restricted?

failure_question: For each unacceptable failure, does the state have enough evidence to set and monitor a recovery expectation?

failure_question: Where does the formal road class fail to match the service promise people actually need?
